about.name: Mohamed Ashraf Eldemerdash
about.whoIAm:
I am a computer science student who enjoys understanding how systems work under the hood. I'm especially interested in building applications that feel intentional, structured, and reliable rather than rushed or improvised.

I like working across different layers of technology from application logic and user interfaces to networking concepts and security fundamentals and I'm constantly experimenting with new tools and ideas through hands-on projects.
whatIDo: Build and test applications and systems
Create arcade and interactive experiences using Unity
Explore security and networking concepts through labs
Learn by experimenting, breaking, and rebuilding systems

projects.intro: Built a controlled internal lab to simulate a real client engagement from recon to reporting. Started with host discovery and service enumeration, then chained misconfigurations into privilege escalation paths.
projects.stack: Kali Linux, Nmap, Metasploit, Burp Suite
projects.title: Internal Network Pentest Lab
projects.details: The project focused on repeatable methodology, evidence collection, and a clean findings narrative for both technical and non-technical audiences.
highlights: Automated scoped scans with Nmap profiles for fast baseline mapping.
Validated exploitable paths in Metasploit and documented proof-of-impact.
Mapped every finding to remediation actions with risk priority.
projects.hotlineOpen: Opened shell project 1: Internal Network Pentest Lab.

projects.intro: Ran a red-team style simulation against a segmented Active Directory lab to test detection and response posture. The operation was designed to emulate realistic operator behavior instead of noisy one-shot exploits.
projects.stack: Kali Linux, GoPhish, C2 Framework, AD Lab
projects.title: Red Team Initial Access Simulation
projects.details: Emphasis was on stealth, lateral movement discipline, and documenting defender blind spots that matter in real incidents.
highlights: Executed phishing-to-access chain with controlled payload execution.
Practiced low-noise privilege escalation and host pivoting sequences.
Delivered timeline-based report with blue-team detection gaps.
projects.hotlineOpen: Opened shell project 2: Red Team Initial Access Simulation.

projects.intro: Developed a post-exploitation playbook in a legal sandbox to evaluate how long operations can stay undetected after foothold. Focused on credential access simulation, beacon shaping, and OPSEC checks.
projects.stack: Kali Linux, Mimikatz Lab, C2 Profiles, Wireshark
projects.title: Post-Exploitation & C2 Tradecraft
projects.details: Captured packet-level traces and host telemetry to compare offensive actions with defensive visibility at each stage.
highlights: Tested encrypted beacon profiles against network monitoring controls.
Compared credential access techniques and their forensic footprint.
Produced hardening recommendations tied to ATT&CK techniques.
projects.hotlineOpen: Opened shell project 3: Post-Exploitation & C2 Tradecraft.

networkingProjects.intro: Designed a segmented campus network model with isolated user, server, and management zones. The focus was reducing lateral movement and keeping broadcast domains controlled without hurting daily operations.
networkingProjects.title: Campus Segmentation Blueprint
networkingProjects.details: Validation covered route flow, policy enforcement at segment boundaries, and failover behavior during link interruptions.
highlights: Created VLAN and subnet plan aligned to department risk profiles.
Implemented ACL rules to enforce least-privilege east-west traffic.
Documented routing and security policy matrix for operations handoff.
networkingProjects.hotlineOpen: Opened networking project 1: Campus Segmentation Blueprint.

networkingProjects.intro: Built a branch simulation with primary and backup WAN paths to test route convergence and service continuity. Prioritized voice and operational traffic under congestion scenarios.
networkingProjects.stack: OSPF, Static Backup Routes, NAT, QoS
networkingProjects.title: Branch-to-HQ Resilient Routing Lab
networkingProjects.details: The project compared dynamic routing recovery against static fallback behavior and measured impact during planned and unplanned outages.
highlights: Tuned OSPF timers and tested reconvergence windows.
Implemented NAT and policy-based prioritization for critical apps.
Produced outage runbook with expected failover sequence.
networkingProjects.hotlineOpen: Opened networking project 2: Branch-to-HQ Resilient Routing Lab.

networkingProjects.intro: Hardened a datacenter-style access layer to reduce misconfiguration risk and suppress common layer-2 attack paths. Combined preventive controls with monitoring hooks for faster incident triage.
networkingProjects.stack: STP Guardrails, Port Security, DHCP Snooping, Logs
networkingProjects.title: Datacenter Access Layer Hardening
networkingProjects.details: Testing focused on rogue device behavior, loop prevention, and assurance that controls did not disrupt normal provisioning workflows.
highlights: Applied BPDU protections and loop guard policies on edge links.
Enabled DHCP snooping and source validation on untrusted ports.
Mapped switch logs into an event checklist for responders.
networkingProjects.hotlineOpen: Opened networking project 3: Datacenter Access Layer Hardening.

arcade.title: ARCADE MODE

projects.title: EcoRun
hotline: EcoRun loaded. Pace and timing are everything here.
Cross-platform build profile active: Desktop / Mobile / Web.
Obstacle cadence synced. Keep your line and avoid branch collisions.
Session note: this build prioritizes stable frame pacing on low-end devices.
projects.narrative: I designed this project to feel immediately readable on any screen size while preserving challenge escalation over long sessions. The visual language and obstacle cadence were tuned to avoid fatigue and keep each run readable at speed.
projects.objective: EcoRun is an endless runner set in a polluted world where momentum and route awareness decide survival. The core fantasy is simple and urgent: collect clean air canisters, avoid hazardous branches, and maintain a rhythm that feels rewarding under pressure.
technical: Cross-platform input and UI adaptation for desktop, mobile, and web.
Collision, movement, and obstacle pacing tuned for endless-loop replayability.
Performance pass for stable gameplay on lower-spec targets.
projects.hotlineHover: EcoRun profile highlighted. Endless loop balancing in focus.

projects.title: Island Escape
hotline: Island Escape loaded. Resource discipline drives progression.
Bridge objective armed. Collect wood, ignore rocks.
Traversal route check: reward comes from clean decision-making, not random pickup.
Camera and movement tuned for exploration readability under pressure.
projects.narrative: The design intent was to combine exploration with deliberate decision-making. Instead of purely collecting everything in sight, the player is rewarded for filtering, planning, and moving with purpose through the environment.
projects.objective: Island Escape is a third-person progression game where resource judgment is the main mechanic: gather enough wood to construct a bridge and advance, while rejecting non-useful pickups that slow your route.
technical: Interactive environment logic for collectible validation and bridge progression.
Third-person camera and movement flow built around exploration clarity.
Obstacle penalty rules and level pacing for consistent challenge.
projects.hotlineHover: Island Escape selected. Resource filtering system ready.

projects.title: Renault AR Experience
hotline: Renault AR loaded. QR session pipeline online.
AR interaction suite ready: doors, lights, seats, and color states.
Tracking stability checks passed for handheld movement and surface detection.
Touch interaction profile is tuned for non-technical users.
projects.narrative: The focus was practical interaction clarity and smooth onboarding. Every interaction was built to feel responsive for non-technical users while still demonstrating robust AR integration and 3D interaction depth.
projects.objective: Renault AR Experience is a mobile-first augmented reality application where users scan a QR code to place a car model in real space and interact with functional vehicle components.
technical: QR-triggered AR session flow with model placement and interaction state handling.
Interactive car controls: doors, seats, lights, and color variations.
UX tuning for stable camera tracking and touch-first interactions.
projects.hotlineHover: Renault AR preview active. Mobile-first interaction stack detected.

projects.title: Garden Care VR
hotline: Garden Care VR loaded. Precision and consistency over speed.
Growth-state simulation active. Keep harmful grass under control.
VR comfort profile active: gentle pacing, tactile cleanup loop, clear feedback.
Plant-state progression is tracking each cleanup action in real time.
projects.narrative: I structured the loop around calm, tactile repetition so player actions feel meaningful without unnecessary complexity. The experience emphasizes comfort, feedback clarity, and natural VR interaction flow.
projects.objective: Garden Care VR is an immersive simulation centered on maintenance gameplay: remove harmful grass, protect healthy growth zones, and manage the garden state through direct interaction.
technical: Immersive object interaction loops for grab/remove actions.
Task-state logic for plant health progression and level completion.
VR comfort and interaction feedback pass for usability.
projects.hotlineHover: Garden Care VR highlighted. Maintenance loop ready.

projects.title: Elsewedy QA Game
hotline: Elsewedy QA loaded. Inspection line running.
Defect filtering protocol online. Accuracy matters.
Inspection rhythm calibrated for repeatable training-style sessions.
Line integrity mode active: flag anomalies early and commit decisions fast.
projects.narrative: This project was designed to translate real QA logic into an interactive workflow. The objective was operational clarity: detect issues quickly, commit confident decisions, and keep line integrity high.
projects.objective: Elsewedy QA Game is a training-focused inspection simulation where the player evaluates moving motors on an assembly line and removes defective units before they pass downstream.
technical: Conveyor inspection loop with pass/fail classification logic.
Real-world QA-inspired workflow translated into interactive gameplay steps.
Designed for training-style repeatability and clear user feedback.
projects.hotlineHover: Elsewedy QA highlighted. Conveyor inspection protocol is armed.

categories.label: Desktop Applications
categories.summary: Standalone tools designed for fast local workflows and practical utility.

projects.name: Encryption Application
projects.description: A Python desktop utility for encrypting, decrypting, and analyzing text with classic ciphers. It combines a simple GUI with practical brute-force and file-handling flows so the tool stays useful beyond basic demos.
projects.repositoryNote: This is a published repository on the public GitHub account.

categories.label: Multi-Tools
categories.summary: Hybrid systems that combine multiple interfaces or utilities in one product surface.

projects.name: SYS CTRL
projects.description: SYS CTRL is a Windows terminal control deck for routine system maintenance. It combines safe temporary-file cleanup, storage inspection, repair tools, application updates, and power controls in a single retro-styled console interface.
projects.repositoryNote: This is a published repository on the public GitHub account.
